# Evaluating LLMs on Conversational Text-to-SQL under Chain Ambiguity and Intent Drift

[All reading notes](../reading-notes.md) · [Catalog entry](../README.md#tide-bench)

**Full paper read · 2026-11-09**

[Original source](https://aclanthology.org/2026.emnlp-main.2454.pdf) · EMNLP 2026 proceedings pp. 55720-55739

**Reading coverage:** Complete Sections 1-7 and limitations; Appendices A-G, all commitment rules, validation checklists, Tables 1-14, compressed construction prompts and agent prompt. Figure 3 encoded plot text supplemented by the complete corresponding Table 13.

## Research question

Execution accuracy alone obscures whether agents identify dependent clarification needs and retract earlier commitments when user intent changes.

## Method

Constructs paired chain-only, drift-only and joint tasks over 514 BIRD anchors. Two binary clarification layers undergo a counterfactual dependency check; SQL-AST commitment differences define value, constraint and projection drift. A reference-conditioned user simulator supplies replies.

## Evaluation

1,542 samples, 12 LLMs, full and L1-primed protocols. Dialogue accuracy requires all submitted queries to execute correctly; layer identification uses simulator routing, while drift recognition measures a non-monotonic change in generated SQL. Five annotators audit 250 triplets.

## What the results support

Both-layer identification is low despite varied asking rates. Non-monotonic query changes are common, but correct post-drift execution is much lower. Joint cases expose persistence of earlier interpretation errors.

## Limits and qualifications

DRR is an AST-change proxy, not evidence the intended retraction was understood. Only two layers, one drift event and chain-then-drift ordering are studied. The human audit is not unanimous for all samples; row-order-insensitive execution and synthesized dialogues bound the findings. Full artifacts remain separately unverified.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

Adds valuable diagnostic protocols for dependency and revision handling without establishing unrestricted conversational reliability.

## Checks against the paper

These are interpretations checked against the source, not verbatim quotations attributed to its authors.

| Claim or inference examined | Original evidence | Location | Assessment |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| High drift recognition means models understand the requested revision. | Rec is defined solely by S(pre) not being a subset of S(post); DRA separately requires post-drift execution correctness. | Section 4.3/Table 2 and Appendix A | Recognition is an operational structural proxy; incorrect changes can satisfy it. |
| The sample construction is fully human validated. | Only 250 triplets are audited; overall majority acceptance 92.4% and strict 83.1%, with joint strict 76.8%. | Section 3.3/Table 1 and Appendix C | Audit supports substantial validity with residual issues, not validation of every item. |
| Projection drift preserves all filtering commitments. | Definition and algorithm require Wpre=Wpost, but compressed generation prompt permits target_change with WHERE column changes and Table 12 shows mean predicate change −0.03. | Section 2.2, Algorithm 1, Appendix G/Table 12, Figure 7 | Unresolved construction-description mismatch; actual released records are needed to reconcile the boundary. |

Reading and source inspection do not establish independent reproduction. Artifact availability is recorded separately in the catalog.
